title: How to modify any training program
summary: NH explains that any program can and should be modified, and that modifying programs is how you learn to program. A program is exercise selection, volume, intensity and frequency: a block of fatigue to be budgeted with additions and subtractions. Swap lifts for equivalents, match the set-rep numbers or justify the change, make small changes and test them in the gym, and take most care with compound lifts.
claims: Any program can be modified; coaches who say touching anything breaks it are ego-driven
Mistakes from modifying a program can't be catastrophic; a bad change punishes you quickly and gets corrected
Modifying a program is learning to program; base your first program on the novice program you run
If the base program is very bad, start from scratch rather than fixing it
A program is just exercise selection, volume, intensity and frequency
Programming is subtraction and addition: when you add something, usually remove something less effective; programs shouldn't be greedy
In his reviews he typically cuts programs by 20-30% because they contain too much
The bench is just a horizontal press; dips or push-ups can replace it with no other change to volume or intensity
When changing set-rep schemes, match total reps (5x5 = 25) or know why you are changing volume; 3x3 plus backoff sets can reach 25
Budget weekly volume: you can cut 30-40% of chest volume if your chest is big, and spend the saved volume on weak areas like shoulders, or on recovery
Any program, even the worst, is a block of fatigue; manage it to get as much as possible from as little as possible
Make small changes first and build up; many changes at once make it impossible to assess them
Test every change in the gym; the body is the best judge of a program's effectiveness
The bigger the muscle group added or removed, the bigger the impact; 3 sets of curls adds no real fatigue, 3 sets of deadlifts does
Compound movements are the hardest to modify because they carry the most tonnage and open the session
Small additions like calves or rear delts barely matter; 5 weekly calf sets over two days won't hurt your squat
Even for small muscles start with 3 weekly sets, then 6, adding a set at a time
You can learn to program in 1.5-3 years, then refine until you reach a final program that doesn't need changes
